title: सर्बियामा विद्यार्थी आन्दोलनको जित, दक्षिणपन्थी पपुलिस्ट राष्ट्रपति भुचिचले स्वीकारे हार
content:
No ads found for this position काठमाडौं । सर्बियामा दुई वर्षदेखि जारी युवा विद्यार्थी नेतृत्वको भ्रष्टाचारविरोधी आन्दोलनले संसदीय चुनावमा जित हासिल गरेको छ। लामो समयदेखि सर्बियाली राजनीतिमा प्रभाव जमाउँदै आएका दक्षिणपन्थी पपुलिस्ट नेता अलेक्जान्दर भुचिचले मध्यावधि संसदीय चुनावमा आफ्नो पार्टी पराजित भएको स्वीकार गरेका छन्। आइतबार राति राजधानी बेलग्रेडस्थित आफ्नो सर्बियन प्रोग्रेसिभ पार्टी (एसएनएस) को मुख्यालयबाट सम्बोधन गर्दै भुचिचले अन्तिम मतपरिणाम सार्वजनिक हुन बाँकी रहे पनि आफ्नो पार्टीले चुनाव हारेको स्पष्ट भएको बताएका हुन्। सर्बियाको निर्वाचन आयोगका प्रारम्भिक तथ्याङ्कले मतदानमा उच्च सहभागिता देखाएको थियो। चुनावअघि राजनीतिक विश्लेषकहरूले ठूलो मतदानले विद्यार्थी आन्दोलनलाई फाइदा पुग्न सक्ने आँकलन गरेका थिए। भुचिचले चुनावमा हार स्वीकार गरेसँगै राजधानी बेलग्रेडसहित विभिन्न सहरमा विद्यार्थी आन्दोलनका समर्थकले उत्सव मनाएका छन्। सडकमा नाचगान, नाराबाजी र आतसबाजी गरिएको थियो। प्रदर्शनकारीहरूले ‘सर्बिया स्वतन्त्र भयो’ भन्दै खुसी व्यक्त गरेका थिए। सन् २०२४ मा उत्तरी सर्बियाको नोभी साद सहरस्थित रेल्वे स्टेसनको छाना खसेर १६ जनाको मृत्यु भएपछि सरकारविरुद्ध विद्यार्थी आन्दोलन चर्किएको थियो। उक्त घटनालाई भ्रष्टाचार, लापरबाही र सरकारी जबाफदेहिताको अभावको प्रतीकका रूपमा लिइएको थियो। त्यसपछि सुरु भएको प्रदर्शनले बिस्तारै देशव्यापी रूप लियो। विद्यार्थीको नेतृत्वमा अघि बढेको आन्दोलनमा भ्रष्टाचारविरोधी समूह र सरकारप्रति असन्तुष्ट मतदाता पनि जोडिए। आन्दोलनको दबाबबीच भुचिचले मध्यावधि संसदीय चुनाव घोषणा गरेका थिए। विद्यार्थी आन्दोलनले चुनावमा उम्मेदवार उठाउने निर्णय गर्दै देशभरका विभिन्न क्षेत्रबाट उम्मेदवार समेटेको थियो। ‘स्टुडेन्ट लिस्ट’ नामक विद्यार्थीसमर्थित चुनावी समूहमा चिकित्सक, कलाकार, प्राध्यापक, खेलकुद क्षेत्रका व्यक्तिसहित विभिन्न पेसा र सामाजिक पृष्ठभूमिका मानिस सहभागी थिए। यस समूहको स्पष्ट र परम्परागत राजनीतिक नेतृत्व संरचना थिएन। यसका धेरै सदस्य प्रत्यक्ष राजनीतिक प्रतिस्पर्धामा अभ्यस्त थिएनन्। स्टुडेन्ट लिस्टका प्रमुख उम्मेदवार इलिया स्र्दानोभिचले बीबीसीसँग कुरा गर्दै यस परिणामले सर्बियालाई स्वतन्त्र राज्य बनाउने आशा व्यक्त गरेका छन्। भ्रष्टाचारविरोधी आन्दोलनले देशलाई ‘अत्याचारबाट मुक्त’ गराउने लक्ष्य राखेको उनले बताए। भुचिच दुई कार्यकाल सर्बियाको राष्ट्रपति भइसकेका नेता हुन्। संवैधानिक व्यवस्थाअनुसार तेस्रो कार्यकालका लागि राष्ट्रपति बन्न नसक्ने भएपछि उनी आफ्नो पार्टीलाई नेतृत्व गर्दै पुनः प्रधानमन्त्री बन्ने लक्ष्यसहित चुनावी प्रतिस्पर्धामा उत्रिएका थिए। उनले सन् २०१७ मा प्रधानमन्त्री पद छाडेका थिए। भुचिच युरोपेली संघ (ईयू) मा सर्बियाको सदस्यता प्रयासका समर्थक भए पनि युक्रेनमाथि रुसको पूर्णस्तरीय आक्रमणपछि मस्कोमाथि प्रतिबन्ध लगाउन अस्वीकार गर्दै आएका छन्। चुनावी अभियानमा उनले पेन्सन र सार्वजनिक क्षेत्रका कर्मचारीको तलब वृद्धि तथा सरकारी स्वास्थ्य सेवामा लगानी बढाउने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरेका थिए। तर, दुई वर्षदेखि जारी भ्रष्टाचारविरोधी आन्दोलन र त्यसबाट बनेको जनमतले उनको पार्टीलाई चुनावी चुनौती दिएको देखिएको छ। Kathmandu. The two-year-old anti-corruption movement led by young students in Serbia has won parliamentary elections. Right-wing populist leader Aleksandar Vucic, who has long influenced Serbian politics, has admitted that his party was defeated in the mid-term parliamentary elections. Speaking from the headquarters of his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) in the capital Belgrade on Sunday night, Vucic said it was clear that his party had lost the election, even though the final results had yet to be announced. Preliminary figures from Serbia's election commission showed a high voter turnout. Before the election, political analysts had predicted that a large turnout would benefit the student movement. Supporters of the student movement celebrated in various cities, including the capital Belgrade, after Vucic conceded defeat in the election. There were dancing, chanting, and fireworks in the streets. The demonstrators expressed their joy by saying, "Serbia is free." Student protests against the government erupted in 2024 after the roof of a railway station in the northern Serbian city of Novi Sad collapsed, killing 16 people. The incident was seen as a symbol of corruption, negligence, and a lack of government accountability. The protests that began then gradually spread nationwide. The student-led movement was joined by anti-corruption groups and voters dissatisfied with the government. Amidst pressure from the protests, Vučić had announced mid-term parliamentary elections. The student movement had decided to field candidates in the elections, including candidates from various regions across the country. The student-backed electoral group called the 'Student List' included people from a variety of professions and social backgrounds, including doctors, artists, professors, and sports figures. The group lacked a clear and traditional political leadership structure. Many of its members were not accustomed to direct political competition. Speaking to the BBC, Student List's lead candidate, Ilija Srdanović, expressed hope that the result would make Serbia an independent state. He said the anti-corruption movement aims to free the country from "tyranny". Vučić, a two-term president of Serbia, is running for re-election as he is constitutionally barred from running for a third term, leading his party to become prime minister again. He stepped down in 2017. Vučić, who supports Serbia's bid for membership in the European Union (EU), has refused to impose sanctions on Moscow following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. During the election campaign, he pledged to increase pensions and public sector salaries and increase investment in public healthcare. However, the two-year-long anti-corruption movement and the public opinion generated by it appear to have posed an electoral challenge to his party.

विद्यार्थी आन्दोलनका समर्थकले उत्सव मनाएका छन्। सडकमा नाचगान, नाराबाजी र आतसबाजी गरिएको थियो। प्रदर्शनकारीहरूले ‘सर्बिया स्वतन्त्र भयो’ भन्दै खुसी व्यक्त गरेका थिए। सन् २०२४ मा उत्तरी सर्बियाको नोभी साद सहरस्थित रेल्वे स्टेसनको छाना खसेर १६ जनाको मृत्यु भएपछि सरकारविरुद्ध विद्यार्थी आन्दोलन चर्किएको थियो। उक्त घटनालाई भ्रष्टाचार, लापरबाही र सरकारी जबाफदेहिताको अभावको प्रतीकका रूपमा लिइएको थियो। त्यसपछि सुरु भएको प्रदर्शनले बिस्तारै देशव्यापी रूप लियो। विद्यार्थीको नेतृत्वमा अघि बढेको आन्दोलनमा भ्रष्टाचारविरोधी समूह र सरकारप्रति असन्तुष्ट मतदाता पनि जोडिए। आन्दोलनको दबाबबीच भुचिचले मध्यावधि संसदीय चुनाव घोषणा गरेका थिए। विद्यार्थी आन्दोलनले चुनावमा उम्मेदवार उठाउने निर्णय गर्दै देशभरका विभिन्न क्षेत्रबाट उम्मेदवार समेटेको थियो। ‘स्टुडेन्ट लिस्ट’ नामक विद्यार्थीसमर्थित चुनावी समूहमा चिकित्सक, कलाकार, प्राध्यापक, खेलकुद क्षेत्रका व्यक्तिसहित विभिन्न पेसा र सामाजिक पृष्ठभूमिका मानिस सहभागी थिए। यस समूहको स्पष्ट र परम्परागत राजनीतिक नेतृत्व संरचना थिएन। यसका धेरै सदस्य प्रत्यक्ष राजनीतिक प्रतिस्पर्धामा अभ्यस्त थिएनन्। स्टुडेन्ट लिस्टका प्रमुख उम्मेदवार इलिया स्र्दानोभिचले बीबीसीसँग कुरा गर्दै यस परिणामले सर्बियालाई स्वतन्त्र राज्य बनाउने आशा व्यक्त गरेका छन्। भ्रष्टाचारविरोधी आन्दोलनले देशलाई ‘अत्याचारबाट मुक्त’ गराउने लक्ष्य राखेको उनले बताए। भुचिच दुई कार्यकाल सर्बियाको राष्ट्रपति भइसकेका नेता हुन्। संवैधानिक व्यवस्थाअनुसार तेस्रो कार्यकालका लागि राष्ट्रपति बन्न नसक्ने भएपछि उनी आफ्नो पार्टीलाई नेतृत्व गर्दै पुनः प्रधानमन्त्री बन्ने लक्ष्यसहित चुनावी प्रतिस्पर्धामा उत्रिएका थिए। उनले सन् २०१७ मा प्रधानमन्त्री पद छाडेका थिए। भुचिच युरोपेली संघ (ईयू) मा सर्बियाको सदस्यता प्रयासका समर्थक भए पनि युक्रेनमाथि रुसको पूर्णस्तरीय आक्रमणपछि मस्कोमाथि प्रतिबन्ध लगाउन अस्वीकार गर्दै आएका छन्। चुनावी अभियानमा उनले पेन्सन र सार्वजनिक क्षेत्रका कर्मचारीको तलब वृद्धि तथा सरकारी स्वास्थ्य सेवामा लगानी बढाउने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरेका थिए। तर, दुई वर्षदेखि जारी भ्रष्टाचारविरोधी आन्दोलन र त्यसबाट बनेको जनमतले उनको पार्टीलाई चुनावी चुनौती दिएको देखिएको छ। Kathmandu. The two-year-old anti-corruption movement led by young students in Serbia has won parliamentary elections. Right-wing populist leader Aleksandar Vucic, who has long influenced Serbian politics, has admitted that his party was defeated in the mid-term parliamentary elections. Speaking from the headquarters of his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) in the capital Belgrade on Sunday night, Vucic said it was clear that his party had lost the election, even though the final results had yet to be announced. Preliminary figures from Serbia's election commission showed a high voter turnout. Before the election, political analysts had predicted that a large turnout would benefit the student movement. Supporters of the student movement celebrated in various cities, including the capital Belgrade, after Vucic conceded defeat in the election. There were dancing, chanting, and fireworks in the streets. The demonstrators expressed their joy by saying, "Serbia is free." Student protests against the government erupted in 2024 after the roof of a railway station in the northern Serbian city of Novi Sad collapsed, killing 16 people. The incident was seen as a symbol of corruption, negligence, and a lack of government accountability. The protests that began then gradually spread nationwide. The student-led movement was joined by anti-corruption groups and voters dissatisfied with the government. Amidst pressure from the protests, Vučić had announced mid-term parliamentary elections. The student movement had decided to field candidates in the elections, including candidates from various regions across the country. The student-backed electoral group called the 'Student List' included people from a variety of professions and social backgrounds, including doctors, artists, professors, and sports figures. The group lacked a clear and traditional political leadership structure. Many of its members were not accustomed to direct political competition. Speaking to the BBC, Student List's lead candidate, Ilija Srdanović, expressed hope that the result would make Serbia an independent state. He said the anti-corruption movement aims to free the country from "tyranny". Vučić, a two-term president of Serbia, is running for re-election as he is constitutionally barred from running for a third term, leading his party to become prime minister again. He stepped down in 2017. Vučić, who supports Serbia's bid for membership in the European Union (EU), has refused to impose sanctions on Moscow following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. During the election campaign, he pledged to increase pensions and public sector salaries and increase investment in public healthcare. However, the two-year-long anti-corruption movement and the public opinion generated by it appear to have posed an electoral challenge to his party.

Preliminary figures from Serbia's election commission showed a high voter turnout. Before the election, political analysts had predicted that a large turnout would benefit the student movement. Student protests against the government erupted in 2024 after the roof of a railway station in the northern Serbian city of Novi Sad collapsed, killing 16 people. The group lacked a clear and traditional political leadership structure. Many of its members were not accustomed to direct political competition. Speaking to the BBC, Student List's lead candidate, Ilija Srdanović, expressed hope that the result would make Serbia an independent state. भुचिच दुई कार्यकाल सर्बियाको राष्ट्रपति भइसकेका नेता हुन्। संवैधानिक व्यवस्थाअनुसार तेस्रो कार्यकालका लागि राष्ट्रपति बन्न नसक्ने भएपछि उनी आफ्नो पार्टीलाई नेतृत्व गर्दै पुनः प्रधानमन्त्री बन्ने लक्ष्यसहित चुनावी प्रतिस्पर्धामा उत्रिएका थिए। उनले सन् २०१७ मा प्रधानमन्त्री पद छाडेका थिए।

भुचिच युरोपेली संघ (ईयू) मा सर्बियाको सदस्यता प्रयासका समर्थक भए पनि युक्रेनमाथि रुसको पूर्णस्तरीय आक्रमणपछि मस्कोमाथि प्रतिबन्ध लगाउन अस्वीकार गर्दै आएका छन्। चुनावी अभियानमा उनले पेन्सन र सार्वजनिक क्षेत्रका कर्मचारीको तलब वृद्धि तथा सरकारी स्वास्थ्य सेवामा लगानी बढाउने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरेका थिए।

तर, दुई वर्षदेखि जारी भ्रष्टाचारविरोधी आन्दोलन र त्यसबाट बनेको जनमतले उनको पार्टीलाई चुनावी चुनौती दिएको देखिएको छ।

Kathmandu. The two-year-old anti-corruption movement led by young students in Serbia has won parliamentary elections. Right-wing populist leader Aleksandar Vucic, who has long influenced Serbian politics, has admitted that his party was defeated in the mid-term parliamentary elections. Speaking from the headquarters of his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) in the capital Belgrade on Sunday night, Vucic said it was clear that his party had lost the election, even though the final results had yet to be announced. Preliminary figures from Serbia's election commission showed a high voter turnout. Before the election, political analysts had predicted that a large turnout would benefit the student movement. Supporters of the student movement celebrated in various cities, including the capital Belgrade, after Vucic conceded defeat in the election. There were dancing, chanting, and fireworks in the streets. The demonstrators expressed their joy by saying, "Serbia is free." Student protests against the government erupted in 2024 after the roof of a railway station in the northern Serbian city of Novi Sad collapsed, killing 16 people. The incident was seen as a symbol of corruption, negligence, and a lack of government accountability. The protests that began then gradually spread nationwide. The student-led movement was joined by anti-corruption groups and voters dissatisfied with the government. Amidst pressure from the protests, Vučić had announced mid-term parliamentary elections. The student movement had decided to field candidates in the elections, including candidates from various regions across the country. The student-backed electoral group called the 'Student List' included people from a variety of professions and social backgrounds, including doctors, artists, professors, and sports figures. The group lacked a clear and traditional political leadership structure. Many of its members were not accustomed to direct political competition. Speaking to the BBC, Student List's lead candidate, Ilija Srdanović, expressed hope that the result would make Serbia an independent state. He said the anti-corruption movement aims to free the country from "tyranny". Vučić, a two-term president of Serbia, is running for re-election as he is constitutionally barred from running for a third term, leading his party to become prime minister again. He stepped down in 2017. Vučić, who supports Serbia's bid for membership in the European Union (EU), has refused to impose sanctions on Moscow following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. During the election campaign, he pledged to increase pensions and public sector salaries and increase investment in public healthcare. However, the two-year-long anti-corruption movement and the public opinion generated by it appear to have posed an electoral challenge to his party.
